source_text: Porro, sicut illud quod de laude dicitur Iudaeorum, non ad hoc valet, ut quisquam genuina credatur sanctitate fulgere; ita etiam quod naturalis malitia vocatur, non ad hoc valet, ut semina vitiosa commendet, sed sine praeiudicio naturae, cuius imperturbabilis ratio est, quae quidquid habet, a Deo suo auctore sortitur, varietas ista verborum, aut invectionis impetum signat, aut laudationis officium.
pass_a_gloss: Further, as that which is said of the praise of the Jews does not avail for this, that anyone be believed to shine with a genuine holiness; so also what is called natural malice does not avail for this, that it commend vicious seeds, but without a prior judgment of nature, whose reason is unperturbed, which whatever it has it receives from God its author, that variety of words either marks the rush of invective or the office of praise.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But just as the praise spoken of the Jews does not mean that anyone should be believed to shine with inborn holiness, so calling malice natural does not mean that the seeds are being declared defective. The constitution of nature is unshakable, and whatever it possesses it receives from God its author. Without counting against that nature, this variety of words marks either the force of rebuke or the work of praise.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
